title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache + parallelism
author: Sophie Kim
description: Motivation: CI workflows have grown monolithic and slow; build matrix duplication and cache churn are increasing queue times. This PR splits the single monorepo workflow into dedicated lint, unit/integration test, and release workflows; consolidates common reusable steps into composite actions; standardizes GitHub Actions versions; improves cache keys and restore/save order; and enables safer parallelism for lint and test jobs. Scope: .github/workflows/*, .github/actions/cache-helpers, package.json (devDeps bump), and small runner config tweaks. Checklist: [x] split workflows, [x] add composite actions, [x] update action versions to v4/v5 where supported, [x] improve cache key semantics to include lockfile hash and job matrix id, [x] validate parallel matrix does not exceed concurrency limits, [x] updated docs and rollout notes. Testing: local act dry-run for actions, staged runs on fork and branch, flaky test quarantine for 72h. Rollout: merge to main, monitor CI queue/median durations for 48h, roll back composite actions if cache hit-rate drops. Related: ENG-2841 for infra perf work and ENG-2902 for release automation hygiene.
commits: split(workflows): move lint/test/release into separate files
feat(actions): add composite action 'ci-common' for setup/caching
chore(deps): bump actions/checkout v4, actions/setup-node v4, actions/cache v4
perf(ci): refine cache key with lockfile-hash and matrix-id
fix(ci): reduce default matrix parallelism to avoid GH concurrency throttling
review_comments: Maya: Please add a note about GH concurrency limits and how we tuned matrix size; resolved after update.
Jordan: Left a comment about cache key ordering - discussed and moved lockfile hash to prefix to avoid stale cache hits.
Evan: Requested smoke-test gating for release workflow; added a required approval job and documented rollback steps.
release_notes: Split CI workflows to improve parallelism and cache hit rates; bumped GH Action versions; added reusable ci-common composite action; no behavioral changes to runtime code.
